title: Bioinformatics and Ecological Risk Classification of Environmental Water Microbiomes
author: Grace Semabia Kpeli
materials: Import quality-controlled, demultiplexed reads into the analysis pipeline.

steps.title: Assign taxonomy with Greengenes
steps.instruction: Map sequencing reads to the Greengenes database version 13.5 to assign taxonomy at kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species levels.

steps.title: Filter and normalize read counts
steps.instruction: Apply read‑count and normalization thresholds to the taxonomic table.

substeps.instruction: Filter: retain taxa with ≥ 500 reads at genus and family levels, and ≥ 100 reads at species level.
Normalize: apply a threshold of 0.5 for genus and family levels and 0.25 for species level.

steps.title: Import and tidy data in RStudio
steps.instruction: Load the taxonomic assignment tables into the RStudio IDE and reformat them into a tidy data structure compatible with ggplot2 and pheatmap workflows.

steps.title: Compute alpha diversity indices
steps.instruction: Calculate alpha‑diversity metrics (Shannon, Simpson, observed species) for each sample using the appropriate R functions.

steps.title: Create diversity visualizations
steps.instruction: Generate diversity plots using ggplot2 and pheatmap, applying the viridis colour palette for accessible, publication‑quality figures.

substeps.instruction: Produce bar/line plots of diversity indices with ggplot2.
Create heatmaps of diversity data with pheatmap.
Apply the viridis colour scale to all figures.

steps.title: Classify microorganisms into risk groups
steps.instruction: Assign every detected microorganism to one of four ecological/risk classes: Healthcare‑associated, Environmental/aquatic, Enteric, or Opportunistic pathogens.

steps.title: Document classification references
steps.instruction: For each organism placed in the Healthcare‑associated, Enteric, or Opportunistic pathogen categories, record the supporting reference or database source used for the classification.

steps.title: Export results to Excel sheets
steps.instruction: Transfer all taxonomic, diversity, and classification results into Microsoft Excel, creating separate worksheets for raw counts, normalized data, diversity metrics, and classification outputs.

steps.title: Generate publication-quality figures
steps.instruction: Produce final figures in RStudio using ggplot2 (bar charts, diversity plots), pheatmap (heatmaps), and viridis (colour scales).

steps.title: Finalize data consistency and reproducibility
steps.instruction: Ensure read‑count and normalization thresholds are applied consistently before any comparative analysis, cross‑reference each classification against at least two independent published sources or databases, and retain raw (pre‑normalization) data files alongside processed files for reproducibility.

substeps.instruction: Verify thresholds applied uniformly across samples.
Save both raw and processed data files.
